ingredients.item: napa cabbage, the crisp stems section, cut into ribbons 1 cm wide
/2 tsp coarse salt , for the 10-minute draw
yuja-cheong — or 1 tbsp honey plus the zest and juice of half a lemon
scallion , sliced; a pinch of black pepper

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: The dressing whisked smooth — gochugaru, yuja, vinegar, soy — into an amber-red slurry that tastes citrus-first, savory-second, with the gochugaru's warmth behind.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a fingertip taste should read like marmalade that went to the grill table: bright, sweet, a warm hum. Sharper or sweeter is a teaspoon of vinegar or yuja away.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: The squeezed cabbage, scallion, and the dressing tossed — spoons this time, gently, the ribbons are sturdy but the toss is short — sesame oil and seeds through.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the eating test: the stem's snap and the citrus dressing's bright-sweet-heat in one bite, with the yuja rind's bitter-edge flick at the finish — the note that separates this slaw from every honey-and-chili imitation. Beside grilled mackerel (#SF07), the fish's fat and the citrus meet exactly as intended.

storageNotes: Best within 2 hours, edible at a day refrigerated (the ribbons hold better than lettuce); undressed salted cabbage keeps half a day.
Variations: matchstick apple folded in for sweetness and snap; the same dressing on cucumber ribbons; a pinch of gochugaru more for the tables that want the slaw to carry heat as well as brightness.
